acceptance_criteria.criterion: Pressing Ctrl+T in a DEBUG build of the app cycles the theme through System → Light → Dark → System in order.
Each cycle persists the new value to `appsettings.json` via `IThemeService` → `ISettingsService`.
The main window's visual theme variant updates immediately on each Ctrl+T press without requiring a relaunch.
The Ctrl+T binding is compiled out of Release builds.

summary: Added IThemeService to MainWindowViewModel constructor; DI resolves it automatically.
Added [RelayCommand] CycleTheme() inside #if DEBUG block in MainWindowViewModel: cycles System→Light→Dark→System via IThemeService.Set.
Added Ctrl+T KeyBinding in MainWindow.axaml.cs inside #if DEBUG, programmatically using Avalonia KeyBinding API with CycleThemeCommand.
Binary verification confirms CycleTheme is absent from Release DLL and present in Debug DLL.
Debug and Release builds both clean with zero warnings.

comments.note: CycleTheme method and its source-generated RelayCommand property are wrapped entirely in #if DEBUG. Binary inspection confirms the symbol is absent from the Release DLL and present in the Debug DLL.

IThemeService is now a required constructor argument for MainWindowViewModel. The DI registration (AddTransient<MainWindowViewModel>) will resolve it automatically via the container. No manual wiring is needed.
The Ctrl+T KeyBinding is added programmatically in MainWindow code-behind inside #if DEBUG. This keeps XAML clean and avoids XAML preprocessor issues (XAML has no #if directive support).

summary: All 4 acceptance criteria verified by code review and automated tests.
VideoIndexer.Tests: 20/20 passed — ThemeService Set_UpdatesCurrent, Set_RaisesThemeChanged_ExactlyOnce, Set_PersistedValue_ReemitsOnReload, Initial_Current_ReflectsSettingsService all pass.

VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests: 21/21 passed — ThemeService suite including Set_PersistsNewModeViaSettingsService, ReInstantiating_ReturnsPersistedTheme, Set_CalledMultipleTimes_RaisesEventEachTime, Set_SameModeAsDefault_StillRaisesEventOnce all pass.
AC4 (compile-out): #if DEBUG guards on both CycleTheme() RelayCommand and KeyBinding in MainWindow code-behind; binary inspection previously confirmed CycleTheme absent from Release DLL.
AC3 (immediate repaint): App.axaml.cs subscribes ThemeChanged → RequestedThemeVariant before MainWindow is constructed; event fires synchronously inside ThemeService.Set().
Cycle order confirmed: System→Light→Dark→System; _ catch-all maps any unknown future mode to System (safe for debug-only code).

comments.note: CycleTheme() switch uses _ catch-all for Dark→System, which also handles any future ThemeMode enum values. Safe for debug-only code but worth noting if the enum grows.
ThemeService.Set() calls SaveAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult() — blocking the UI thread. Class docs acknowledge this is intentional (write is <1KB on explicit user action). No issue at current scale.

No dedicated ViewModel-level unit test for CycleTheme cycle order (System→Light→Dark→System) — coverage relies on ThemeService tests. Acceptable since CycleTheme is debug-only scaffolding, not production logic.

summary: All 4 acceptance criteria met and confirmed by code inspection.

`#if DEBUG` guards are correctly placed in both files: (1) the `using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.Input;` import and the entire `CycleTheme()` method in MainWindowViewModel.cs, (2) the `KeyBindings.Add(...)` block in MainWindow.axaml.cs. Release builds compile both without any debug symbols.
Cycle order (System→Light→Dark→System) is implemented via an exhaustive switch expression. The `_` catch-all correctly maps Dark→System and is future-safe if the ThemeMode enum gains new values.

MVVM layering is clean: the View binds to `viewModel.CycleThemeCommand` (source-generated from the `[RelayCommand]`-annotated `private CycleTheme()`) — theme service is not accessed directly from the View.
Programmatic KeyBinding in code-behind is the correct Avalonia approach; XAML has no preprocessor directive support.

DI wiring is consistent: `IThemeService` is singleton and `MainWindowViewModel` is transient — correct for a single-window app. Shared singleton ThemeService ensures no state divergence across transient VM instances.
No memory leaks: the KeyBinding is held by the window's own `KeyBindings` collection with lifetime matching the window. No orphaned event subscriptions.
No security, correctness, or maintainability concerns identified.

comments.note: MainWindow.axaml.cs: The parameterless and DI constructors are both `public`. The DI constructor could be `internal` with `[assembly: InternalsVisibleTo(...)]` to prevent accidental direct instantiation outside the app entry point. Not a concern for a single-project desktop app, but worth noting if the project grows to multiple assemblies.
MainWindowViewModel.cs: `CycleTheme()` is `private` — the correct accessibility for a `[RelayCommand]` method; the source generator exposes the public `CycleThemeCommand` property. No issue.
No issues found — code is clean, minimal, and consistent with the project's existing patterns.

notes: All 4 ACs met. Both Debug and Release build cleanly. Binary verified: CycleTheme absent from Release, present in Debug.
